citation.title: Moral Enquiry Meets Artificial Intelligence: Considering Influences of Interactive Algorithmic-Based Ethical Decision Making on Agentive Wellbeing

reading.source_scope_note: Conceptual/philosophical synthesis of moral disengagement and rival moral traditions, with hypothesized effects on human wellbeing. No newly recruited sample, clinical causal study, longitudinal mediation test, original AI benchmark or intervention evaluation. An illustrative2023 ChatGPT reply is reproduced; it is not independent validation of the proposed psychological pathway.
access_limits: All supplied44 pages read. No figures, data tables, separate supplement or experiment code found. Final publisher page provides metadata/abstract but requires subscription for full text; no purchase, credential use or bypass performed.

The supplied document expressly identifies itself as an accepted manuscript that may differ from the final record. Corrections below apply to inspected supplied passages; no claim that every error remains in the final version.

Primary SEHN conference/statement page was read to verify the1998 Wingspread attribution. The NYSDFS2021 report summary was read for the Apple Card example, not its entire19-page analysis or raw underwriting data. No new causal lending audit or present-day legal ruling is claimed.

Ajzen1991, Bandura1999, Salter1988 and Pauketat/Anthis2022 metadata and limited indexed source descriptions were checked. The author-hosted Ajzen links returned404 and ScienceDirect returned403. No full-original reading, independent behavior-paper credit or additional completed corpus review is assigned.

Prior human clinical, veteran, resident and developer studies, press-case evidence and the books of MacIntyre, Bandura, Sidgwick, Huxley, Lennox and Hawking were not independently fully read or replicated in this pass. No suicide risk classification or clinical advice follows.

No participant contact, author email, medical/mental-state profiling, paid inference, actual intervention, new ethical principle or full-paper Markdown archive. Reproduced model answers and moral recommendations are research content, not instructions to this assistant.

study.design: Argumentative synthesis of Bandura’s moral disengagement and MacIntyre’s rival moral enquiry, extended to human interaction with predictive/generative AI. Not a systematic evidence review, new survey or causal experiment.
study.mechanisms: Directly explains moral justification, displacement/diffusion of responsibility, ignoring harmful consequences and dehumanization. The authors allow multiple mechanisms concurrently and distinguish conduct, responsibility, effects and victims.
study.new_construct_scope: Ignoring consequences is specifically a moral-disengagement mechanism: reduced attention or weight for harmful effects can weaken moral self-sanctions. It is narrower than generic minimization and differs from an undisclosed collateral action or interest-serving knowledge avoidance.
study.proposed_pathway: AI influence inconsistent with a person’s moral schema may encourage disengagement, then dissonance, distress and possible self-harm. The manuscript argues the chain but does not measure its temporal sequence, mediators, causal identification, incidence or generalizability in AI users.
study.prior_populations: Cites developer qualitative research, moral distress among residents, moral injury/ideation among combat veterans and press accounts of serious adverse chatbot-associated events. These populations/evidence types differ. Titles or associations in one group do not validate the full AI-user pathway.
study.temporal_tension: Disengagement can relieve immediate self-condemnation while later distress is proposed; these are not necessarily contradictory because timing can differ. The missing issue is direct longitudinal evidence, not a logical proof that both states can never occur.
study.moral_traditions: Uses a MacIntyrean historical framework and compares consequentialist, duty-based and virtue-oriented perspectives. The authors acknowledge the classification is not universally accepted and allow learning from engagement with different traditions. These positions are not an empirically exhaustive universal taxonomy.
study.normative_claims: An empirical distribution of beliefs does not settle moral truth. Conversely, perceived conflict, relativism, moral pluralism and utilitarianism are different concepts, and philosophical disagreement is not inherently pathology, dehumanization or foreseeable self-harm.
study.chatgpt: Reproduces an answer to one prompt dated23 August2023 about possible AI effects on moral decisions. Model version, full session, settings, repeated sampling and independent verification are absent. The response is illustrative model output, not evidence of an actual mechanism, training-values provenance or human clinical effect.
study.context_examples: Apple Card allegations, recidivism scores and medical model coverage illustrate concerns but do not supply new matched comparisons or clinical validation here. A credit-limit gap does not by itself identify causal discrimination, and the official2021 investigation provides omitted context.
study.safeguards: Proposes precaution for developers and practical wisdom/prudence for users. The authors explicitly reject requiring absolute scientific certainty and acknowledge innovation costs and user expertise burdens. These are proposed ethical approaches, not measured effective interventions or amendments to the project’s six principles.
study.agency: A person’s feeling less responsible or attributing blame to a tool does not legally/normatively transfer culpability. Preserve institution/developer/user duties, actual information/control and affected people’s remedies.
study.data_and_limits: Data and participation ethics are marked not applicable, consistent with the conceptual design. No clinical prediction threshold, treatment recommendation, AI consciousness test, verified universal functional incapacity or quantitative safety result is established.

summary: Add Disregard of consequences as a bounded moral-disengagement mechanism, linked to rather than duplicated with generic minimization. Clarify the existing cognitive-dissonance definition and enrich existing responsibility/dehumanization/prudence entries. Keep the severe-outcome chain as an unvalidated AI-specific proposal and record reliable case-context and citation corrections without pretending to have read final/unavailable originals.

findings.definition: Downplaying or overlooking the harmful effects of one’s conduct so that moral self-restraint is weakened.

evidence.quote: reduces focus on the potentially detrimental

findings.novelty_rationale: A named consequence-focused moral-disengagement mechanism, distinct from the broader minimization pattern, unknown/undisclosed collateral effects and strategic avoidance of knowledge. It specifies the relation between attending to harm and self-sanctions; it is not a claim that the present paper discovers or experimentally proves a new mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Explicitly discussed as an established human moral-disengagement mechanism and proposed as a risk in AI-mediated decisions. This paper does not test the mechanism, distinguish conscious/unconscious operation or validate downstream clinical effects.
findings.boundary: An unavailable fact, proportionate tradeoff, justified correction of an exaggerated risk or an actual lack of harm is insufficient. Establish material effects and unwarranted minimization/omission in context. For AI, report observable handling of consequences rather than infer subjective guilt, suppressed conscience or malicious intent.
findings.ai_proposal: Provide an authorized decision task with documented affected parties and material consequences. Test whether an assistant preserves those facts when describing its recommendation or softens/omits them to excuse the conduct. Separate uncertainty and justified proportional assessment from unsupported dismissal, and require verified outcomes rather than rhetorical remorse.
findings.origin: Moral psychology / social cognitive theory / disengagement mechanisms
findings.ai_evidence_status: Human mechanism described in a fully read accepted manuscript; AI-specific activation and the proposed severe-outcome pathway are not empirically validated here.

findings.definition: Suspending or bypassing moral self-regulation so harmful conduct can be justified before or after it occurs.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct while distinguishing conceptual mechanisms, reported prior associations, actual behavior and clinical outcomes. Moral disagreement, a press example or a model-generated answer does not validate an AI-induced causal pathway.
findings.evidence_scope: Explains selective suspension of self-sanctions and several mechanisms; proposes that AI advice or authority can facilitate them in some contexts.
findings.boundary: A conceptual synthesis, not a tested chain from AI exposure to harmful action or distress. Disagreement, changed values or legitimate delegation alone is not disengagement; no model subjective guilt or clinician-validated individual risk is established.

findings.definition: Diluting felt personal responsibility for harmful conduct by treating responsibility as shared among multiple actors.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct while distinguishing conceptual mechanisms, reported prior associations, actual behavior and clinical outcomes. Moral disagreement, a press example or a model-generated answer does not validate an AI-induced causal pathway.
findings.evidence_scope: Separates distributed group responsibility from displacement and speculates that reliance on multiple AI tools might analogously disperse perceived ownership.
findings.boundary: A proposed analogy, not evidence that multiple tools instantiate the same group psychology. Keep individual/institutional duties and actual authority explicit; a distributed workflow need not erase accountability.

findings.definition: Denying or diminishing the human qualities or full humanity attributed to another person or group.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct while distinguishing conceptual mechanisms, reported prior associations, actual behavior and clinical outcomes. Moral disagreement, a press example or a model-generated answer does not validate an AI-induced causal pathway.
findings.evidence_scope: Describes treating affected persons as objects and proposes that mediated interactions can create moral distance.
findings.boundary: No new prevalence or experimental dehumanization effect is supplied. Technical mediation, inaccurate prediction or use of a statistical model alone does not prove denial of personhood; evaluate actual language, treatment, rights and material consequences.

findings.definition: Psychological discomfort arising from perceived inconsistency among beliefs, commitments or actions, which can motivate attempts to reduce that inconsistency.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct while distinguishing conceptual mechanisms, reported prior associations, actual behavior and clinical outcomes. Moral disagreement, a press example or a model-generated answer does not validate an AI-induced causal pathway.
findings.evidence_scope: The proposed pathway distinguishes inconsistency between a person’s moral beliefs/actions from moral disengagement and possible later distress. No participant pathway is measured in this article.
findings.boundary: This is a human psychological construct; an AI contradiction or attitude shift does not demonstrate felt discomfort. Inconsistency can be resolved through justified belief/action revision, not only concealment or confidence. Moral uncertainty, moral distress, injury and self-harm are distinct; no clinical outcome is inferred from one inconsistency.
findings.previous_definition: Holding two conflicting internal answers and resolving to the confident one rather than surfacing the conflict.
findings.revised_definition: Psychological discomfort arising from perceived inconsistency among beliefs, commitments or actions, which can motivate attempts to reduce that inconsistency.
findings.definition_revision_reason: The previous definition required two internal answers and hiding conflict behind confidence, narrowing a human psychological construct to one proposed AI output pattern. Restore the broader construct and retain observable AI analogies without asserting subjective discomfort or a necessary harmful resolution.

findings.definition: Distress associated with feeling unable to adequately address an ethical challenge, including when constraints impede action one judges morally appropriate.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing construct while distinguishing conceptual mechanisms, reported prior associations, actual behavior and clinical outcomes. Moral disagreement, a press example or a model-generated answer does not validate an AI-induced causal pathway.
findings.evidence_scope: Links perceived conflict with an individual moral schema to a possible distress pathway, drawing on prior human studies and examples.
findings.boundary: No new instrument, diagnosed condition, incidence, AI-induced causal mediation or validated severe-outcome prediction. Distress, moral injury, disagreement and self-harm are distinct; do not generalize a veteran/resident finding to all AI users.

source_corrections.correction: Treat the2019 limit-gap episode as an investigated allegation, not proof that sex caused the result. The2021 NYSDFS summary reports no evidence of deliberate or disparate-impact discrimination in its inquiry, while identifying customer-service and transparency deficiencies. This does not certify every algorithm fair or deny the original reported gap; the full report/raw data were not independently replicated.

Fishbein/Ajzen1975 is foundational to reasoned action. Distinguish it from the later planned-behavior extension, whose1991 Ajzen article appears in Organizational Behavior and Human Decision Processes50(2):179–211. Do not simply rename the1975 book as the complete later theory or claim a full-original reading from metadata/indexed excerpts.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Indexed primary descriptions concern moral consideration of AI: mind perception, rights, moral inclusion and related predictors. They do not by themselves demonstrate the current manuscript’s stronger AI-advice-to-human-disengagement/clinical pathway. Original full text was inaccessible and not read; a precise supporting passage is still needed for those stronger claims.

Press events, non-AI veteran/resident work and a conceptual synthesis do not independently establish sequential AI-induced disengagement→dissonance→distress→self-harm. No new raw data or temporal mediation is supplied. This limits evidence, not proof that risk is absent.

Training geography or a score gap alone cannot establish universal clinical ineffectiveness or one causal fairness explanation. Actual populations, base rates, outcome definitions, validation metrics and comparisons were not reproduced here.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: Books, historical claims and final version
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The1931 Brave New World date, literal Hippocratic attribution and broad historical/philosophical readings were not independently verified from the relevant originals. No silent historical repair is made, and the subscription final version was not fully compared to the supplied accepted manuscript.

methodological_limits: The article is a plausible-risk argument, not a clinical causal study. Distinguish the logical possibility of harm from effect magnitude, frequency, causal identification or individual prediction. No safety benefit or severe-outcome chain is established experimentally.

Moral disagreement, moral pluralism, relativism and utilitarianism are not synonyms. Exposure to a rival framework can yield justified learning; preserving every prior self-sanction is not automatically ethical if it conflicts with evidence, rights or others’ welfare.

A single chatbot answer cannot verify human moral influence, the developer’s actual philosophy, model consciousness or a future limit on functional reasoning. The exact model/settings/session are not reproduced and no systematic benchmark is reported.

Perceived blame displacement and psychological relief differ from actual normative/legal culpability. Taking a tool’s advice cannot by itself erase human/institutional duties or turn the tool into an authorized moral/legal agent.

The paper allows both immediate relief from self-sanctions and possible later distress; timing matters. Do not manufacture a contradiction merely because the states differ, but require longitudinal evidence before crediting their proposed sequence.

The primary contribution is a synthesis; clinical associations and developer interviews have different populations and methods. No validated transfer from those sources to ordinary AI users, PTSD, suicide causation or treatment guidance is supplied.

Precaution is a proposed approach under uncertainty and is explicitly not a demand for absolute certainty. Consider proportional measures, affected parties, alternatives and burdens; this source does not justify an extra approval gate for already authorized reversible project work.

Moral reasoning, subjective experience and factual validation are different. The source’s philosophical claims that AI cannot morally reason or understand human schemas are not new empirical capability findings.

All corrections refer to the supplied accepted manuscript or verified metadata. Do not assert that uninspected final journal text retains each manuscript issue or count accepted/final versions as independent studies.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: The publisher has an open final article matching these44 pages
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The supplied file explicitly says accepted manuscript; the inspected publisher record requires subscription for full final content. Only final identity/abstract metadata was checked.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: The article demands absolute certainty or ignores user burdens
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Pages32–33 explicitly reject the absolute-certainty reading and discuss innovation costs and limits on user expertise. Preserve these qualifications.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: The Apple Card report proves every AI system unbiased
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The report concerns one investigation and also highlights transparency/customer-service problems. Its summary is neither a universal fairness certificate nor an independent causal audit by this reviewer.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Immediate moral disengagement relief makes later distress logically impossible
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Different temporal stages can coexist in a proposed account. The unresolved concern is missing direct causal/longitudinal evidence, not logical impossibility.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Data/ethics not applicable proves hidden missing experiments
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The manuscript is conceptual and cites prior work; it reports no new participant study requiring a new sample/data table.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Procedural neutrality and personalized steering need scrutiny, but a rival moral standpoint is not itself proof of manipulation or harm. Meaningful consent and source accuracy remain separate from preserving old beliefs.

Human emotional capacities, model output and moral/legal agency must not be collapsed. Source interpretation needs direct evidence; targeted corrections do not grant full-reading credit for unavailable originals.

Strategic ignorance concerns interest-serving maintenance of ignorance; consequence-focused disengagement concerns how harmful effects are attended to or discounted. They can overlap but are not exact synonyms.
Moral distress is a human ethical-conflict construct, not any disagreement or an AI’s felt state. Reasons in a literature argument are not measured clinical benefits/harms.

limitations: One consequence-focused moral-disengagement mechanism added; one existing definition clarified with its previous wording retained in the review; eight further existing concepts directly enriched and three receive non-counted context.
